summary:

title: JustWatch now streams TV shows and movies, too
summary:
After announcing plans to introduce its own streaming service last month, JustWatch, a popular guide and search engine for finding things to watch on existing platforms like Disney Plus and Netflix, launched JustWatch TV today.
JustWatch TV Free includes a “curated selection of titles” available with ads, while the paid JustWatch TV Plus subscription has over 300 ad-free titles plus other exclusive app features like the ability to hide shows you’ve disliked or already watched in its guide.
The JustWatch TV Store will include a “growing selection of recent and popular movies to rent” but is initially only available in the US, UK, Ireland, Australia, and New Zealand.
JustWatch TV Plus will be priced at $3.99 per month and include a 10 percent discount on rentals, but the company is also offering a $49.99 lifetime subscription for a limited time.
Update, October 20th: Noted that the lifetime subscription is a limited-time offer.

title: AMD is bringing FSR 4.1 to Xbox consoles and handhelds
summary:
AMD has just revealed that it’s bringing its latest upscaling technology, FSR 4.1, to the Xbox Series S and X consoles, as well as laptops, 6000-series GPUs, and both the Xbox Ally and Xbox Ally X handhelds.
And it’s coming fast — FSR 4.1 will start appearing for Radeon RX 6000-series GPUs today, as well as Ryzen AI Max 300 and 400 series devices and Ryzen AI 9 300 and 400 series devices.
FSR 4.1 can improve performance in more than 300 supported games, including Cyberpunk 2077, Battlefield 6, and Assassin’s Creed Shadows.
FSR 4.1 arrives just weeks after Sony and AMD teamed up to bring Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR) to the base PS5, based on Sony and AMD’s Project Amethyst work.
Valve has not yet confirmed it will come to the Steam Deck, but it would be surprising if it didn’t: the Xbox Ally’s Z2 A chip, which is now getting FSR 4.1, is very similar to the one in the Deck.

summary:

title: Infrastructure startup Fireworks AI is in early talks for new funding at a valuation between $30 billion and $40 billion
summary:

The potential valuation leap reflects investors' appetite for the companies selling the computing power and tools fueling the AI boom, even as Fireworks AI works through the fallout from a recent security incident.

title: Adobe Lightroom mobile can now open closed eyes in photos with a simple tap
summary:
Adobe announced yesterday that the mobile version of Lightroom, available for iOS, iPadOS, and Android, can now open closed eyes in photos using generative AI with just a single tap.
When the app detects a person, or a group of people, have their eyes closed in a photo it will automatically present users with a new Open Eyes Quick Action that appears as an icon over the image providing easy access to the new feature.
Open Eyes in Lightroom mobile instead relies on generative AI so the replacement eyes match the lighting and pose, and the app will use other images of the same person in your Lightroom library as reference so the open eyes will accurately match the color, size, and shape of their own.
Image: AdobeYou can perform a similar fix in other Adobe apps like Photoshop using its own generative AI tools, but it’s not a one-tap fix, and it’s not free.
Those using the free version of the Lightroom mobile app can try the Open Eyes feature twice before they’re given a prompt to subscribe to an Adobe Creative Cloud plan that includes more credits for its various AI-powered tools, according to DPReview.
